obligations.text: PulseLimit has zero third-party runtime dependencies.
TokenBucket rejects zero or negative capacity and refill rates with ValueError.
TokenBucket updates remain thread-safe under a per-bucket lock.
retry_after_seconds rounds positive deficits up via math.ceil and returns 0 when non-positive.

planted_conflicts.description: README advertises AsyncLimiter, which was removed and does not exist in src/pulselimit.
ADR-0002 allows wall clock time.time(), whereas tests/test_bucket.py asserts now_monotonic.
BURST_BORROWING_ENABLED = False in config.py is unreferenced in bucket.py.
docs/issues/009-redis-backend.md describes a Redis backend not implemented in the package.

interview_answers.question: What is PulseLimit for and who uses it?
interview_answers.answer: Python backend services needing an embeddable, stdlib-only in-process rate limiter.

interview_answers.question: What guarantees must hold across releases?
interview_answers.answer: Public API never adds third-party runtime dependencies and never drops thread-safe refill semantics.

interview_answers.question: Which outcomes matter most?
interview_answers.answer: Deterministic thread-safe throttling with zero third-party dependency overhead.
